To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the evolution of wear, corrosion and mechanical damage at the modular taper contact is highly dependent on the type of materials, the surface condition, contact geometry and the environmental conditions.
fretting corrosion of the modular taper interface is dependent on the type of material, the contact condition and location of the fretting wear product within the contact.
the fretting corrosion of metal metal and ceramic-metal interfaces of modular taper is a result of complex interplay between wear, corrosion and mechanical factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of fretting corrosion and the role of multiple factors that contributes to the process.
the understanding of the mechanisms of fretting corrosion and the role of surface history in the evolution of frettings corrosion currents.
the development of an in vitro model that can be used to investigate the evolution of wear, corrosion and mechanical damage at modular taper interface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fretting corrosion at a metal metal interface involves a complex interaction between the mechanical and electrochemical processes.
the fretting contact between CoCrMo and CoCrMo or Ti6Al4v alloys results in a fretting corrosion regime which is dominated by the fretting wear of the CoCrM0 surface.

the fretting and crevic corrosion damage at the modular taper interfaces are a result of a combination of factors including the material properties, the contact geometry, the contact condition and surface history.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evolution of wear, corrosion and metallurgical transformations are dependent on the material and the type of contact.

, the evolution of frettings corrosion at the metal metal interface is governed by the mechanical and electrochemical properties of the materials in contact, the surface topography and the surface condition of the materials.
the use of a metal metal interface is more favourable than a ceramic metal interface for reducing fretting corrosion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fretting corrosion is not a simple phenomenon and that it involves several mechanisms that are interdependent on the type and nature of the materials used in the contact.
the use of metal metal taper interface in total hip arthro plasty (THA), is a better choice than ceramic metal taper interface as it is less susceptible to fretting corrosion.
the evolution of wear, fretting and crevices are interdependent and therefore cannot be studied in isolation.
